runs.answer:
Inflation is when things slowly get more expensive over time.

Imagine a candy bar costs 50 cents today. If prices go up with inflation, that same candy bar might cost 55 cents next year. Your 50 cents can buy a little less candy than it could before.

Why does it happen? Usually because more people want to buy things than there are things to sell, or because it costs businesses more to make things. When that happens, stores raise their prices a bit.

A little inflation is normal, and it happens in most places most years. It just means the money in your piggy bank doesn't buy quite as much as it used to.

Inflation is when things slowly get more expensive over time.

Imagine a candy bar that cost 50 cents when your parents were kids. Today that same candy bar might cost $1.50. The candy bar didn't change, but the money got "weaker," so you need more of it to buy the same thing.

That's inflation. It usually happens a little bit every year, and it's why a dollar today can buy less than a dollar could buy long ago.
